Mr. 1, 1.''}}* he came into al the countrie of Iordan, preaching the bapti{{ls}}me of {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Penance prepareth the way to Chri{{ls}}t.}}∷ penance vnto remi{{ls}}sion of {{ls}}innes: as it is vvritten in the booke of the {{ls}}ayings of E{{ls}}ay the Prophet: {{verse|chapter=3|verse=4}} {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''E{{ls}}a. 40, 3.''}}* ''A voice of one crying in the de{{ls}}ert: prepare the vvay of our Lord, make {{ls}}traight his pathes''. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=5}} ''Euery valley {{ls}}hal be filled: and euery mountaine and hil {{ls}}hal be made lovv, and crooked things {{ls}}hal become {{ls}}traight: and rough vvaies, plaine'': {{verse|chapter=3|verse=6}} ''and al fle{{ls}}h {{ls}}hal {{ls}}ee the {{sc|Salvation}} of God''.

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=7}} He {{ls}}aid therfore to the multitudes that vvent forth to be baptized of him, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 3, 7.''}}* Ye vipers broodes, vvho hath {{ls}}hewed you to flee from the vvrath to come? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=8}} Yeld therfore {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Fruites of penance be workes {{ls}}atisfactorie.}}∷ fruites vvorthie of penance. and doe ye not begin to {{ls}}ay, VVe haue Abraham to our father. For I tel you, that God is able of the{{ls}}e {{ls}}tones to rai{{ls}}e vp children to Abraham. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=9}} And novv the axe is put to the roote of the trees. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ A man without good workes is vnfruitful, and {{ls}}hal be ca{{ls}}t into euerla{{ls}}ting fire.}}∷ Euery tree therfore that yeldeth not good fruite, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`is''}}`{{ls}}hal be' cut dovvne, and ca{{ls}}t into fire. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=10}} And the multitudes a{{ls}}ked him, {{ls}}aying, VVhat {{ls}}hal we doe then? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=11}} And he an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aid vnto them: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Almes coun{{ls}}eled or enioyned for {{ls}}innes and to auoid damnation.}}∷ He that hath tvvo coates, let him giue to him that hath not: and he that hath meate, let him doe likevvi{{ls}}e. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=12}} And the Publicans al{{ls}}o came to be baptized, and {{ls}}aid to him, Mai{{ls}}ter, vvhat {{ls}}hal vve doe? {{verse|chapter=3|verse=13}} But he {{ls}}aid to them, Doe nothing more then that vvhich is appointed you. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=14}} And the {{ls}}ouldiars al{{ls}}o a{{ls}}ked him, {{ls}}aying, VVhat {{ls}}hal vve al{{ls}}o doe? And he {{ls}}aid to them, Vexe not neither calumniate any man: and be content vvith your {{ls}}tipends.

{{verse|chapter=3|verse=15}} And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Iohn was {{ls}}o holy that many might by errour ea{{ls}}ily thinke he was Chri{{ls}}t.}}∷ the people imagining, and al men thinking in their harts of Iohn, le{{ls}}t perhaps he vvere Chri{{ls}}t: {{verse|chapter=3|verse=16}} Iohn an{{ls}}wered, {{ls}}aying vnto al, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 3, 11. Mr. 1, 8.''}}* I in deede baptize you vvith vvater: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 1, 26. Act. 1, 5. 11, 16. 19, 4.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ How {{ls}}ay then the Heretikes that the Bapti{{ls}}me of Chri{{ls}}t is of no greater vertue then Iohns?}}∷ but there {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''`cometh''}}`{{ls}}hal come' a mightier then I, vvho{{ls}}e latchet of his {{ls}}hoes I am not vvorthie to vnloo{{ls}}e, he {{ls}}hal baptize you in the Holy Gho{{ls}}t and fire. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=17}} vvho{{ls}}e fanne is in his hand, and he vvil purge his floore: and vvil gather the vvheate into his barne, but the chaffe he vvil burne vvith vnquencheable fire. {{verse|chapter=3|verse=18}} Many other things al{{ls}}o exhorting did he euangelize to the people.<noinclude>{{rh|||And}}</noinclude>
